newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend slight fall, seen dipping.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend slight fall, seen dipping.

text.p: Polish shares fell slightly for the fourth straight session and analysts said the market should stay flat or slightly down for most of this week as investors take profits after the recent 38-percent surge.

"The flat-to-slightly-downward tendency should continue but we should see a return to growth after the market calms and some investors take profits," said Emil Onyszczuk, a trader at Polish Development Bank (PBR) brokerage.
Some analysts said the bourse would soon rebound as long as foreign exchanges stay strong, while others said it was not yet clear what would happen after the current slight downtrend.
The main market's all-share WIG index eased 0.3 percent to 18,090.8 points and turnover fell 18.4 percent to 165.8 million zlotys on both markets.

Analysts said February 11-20 food price data due on Friday would likely not affect the market as the central bank, before changing rates, was waiting to see the results on inflation of its recent decision to raise banks' obligatory reserves.
The move takes effect on February 28.
Analysts said biggest loser Optimus fell the daily maximum 10 percent in profit-taking.

Analysts said garment makers Wolczanka, Vistula VIS.WA and Prochnik, which gained 10 percent, 8.1 percent and 5.6 percent respectively, were rising after looking relatively undervalued after a poor 1996 on the bourse.
They said Espebepe enjoyed a 9.7-percent speculative surge before its creditors meet on March 14 to discuss the firm's debts.
NFI units rose 0.6 percent to 167 zlotys in 53.9 million-zloty trade and rose 2.4 percent to 171 zlotys in 69.3-million-zloty live trade, where most stocks closed lower in 23.7-million-zloty trade.
